message.content:
**The Kiss** by Auguste Rodin (1889) is widely regarded as the most iconic and celebrated sculpture of the 19th century. ### Why it stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a leading figure of modern sculpture | | **Date** | 1889 (completed in the late 19th century) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist, capturing intimate human emotion | | **Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums worldwide.
• Its fame was amplified by its reproduction in various media (prints, postcards, films). | | **Legacy** | • Continues to be one of the most reproduced and recognized sculptures globally.
• Frequently cited in discussions of 19th‑century art and the transition to modernism. | ### Other notable 19th‑century sculptures - **The Gates of Hell** (1880–1908) – an ambitious monumental work by Rodin, still unfinished but highly influential. - **The Thinker** (1902) – technically early 20th century, but often associated with Rodin’s 19th‑century style and legacy. - **The Birth of Venus** (by various artists, e.g., Alexandre Cabanel, 1863) – a popular academic piece reflecting 19th‑century tastes. While many masterpieces exist, **Rodin’s *The Kiss*** remains the most universally recognized and celebrated sculpture from the 19th century.
